fire/plane: Here are the linear classifier's cats and ships, and the line between them. The score, w dot x plus b, is positive on the ships' side, negative on the cats' side, and grows with the distance from the line.
fire/cell: A brain cell, called a neuron, works differently. It adds up the signals arriving from other cells, and either fires or stays silent.
fire/mp: In 1943, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts turned that into a precise model: a cell fires, all or nothing, once enough of its inputs fire together. That cutoff is its threshold.
fire/flat: An artificial neuron borrows the idea, and the name. It computes the same score, but outputs zero wherever the score is zero or below: the whole cats' side goes silent.
fire/slice: Walk straight across the line. The score was a straight ramp, dipping below zero. Now it lies flat at zero, then climbs past the line: a ramp with a bend.
fire/detector: So this neuron detects ships. It is silent for every cat, however cat-like, and fires for ships, more strongly the farther they are from the line.
bend/z: Give the score a name, z: z equals w dot x plus b. It is the pre-activation: the number before the bend.
bend/a: What comes out is the neuron's activation, written A: how strongly it fires. Below zero, A is zero. Above zero, A is z itself.
bend/max: As a formula, A equals the max of zero and z: the larger of zero and z. So a z of minus two gives zero.
bend/relu: This bend is called the ReLU, short for rectified linear unit, and each word of the name means something.
bend/rect: In electronics, a rectifier lets current through in one direction only. Feed it a wave, and the negative halves are cut off at zero, just as the ReLU cuts off negative z.
bend/linear: Linear, because what passes, passes unchanged: above zero, the graph is the straight line where A equals z.
bend/unit: And unit is another word for a neuron. Strictly, a rectified linear unit is a neuron with this bend, though today ReLU names the bend itself, too.
inside/x: Now in numbers, inside one neuron. It takes an input, x, with two entries: two and one.
inside/w: Each entry has its own weight in w: one, and minus three. A negative weight pulls the sum down, so that input argues against firing.
inside/sum: Multiply and add: two times one, plus one times minus three, is minus one.
inside/b: Then add the bias, two, and z comes out as one.
inside/a: One is above zero, so the ReLU passes it unchanged. The activation is one, and the neuron fires.
inside/neg: Feed it one and two instead. One, minus six, plus two is minus three, and the ReLU turns that into zero. The neuron stays silent.
inside/thr: Here is the threshold again. z is above zero exactly when w dot x is above minus b, here minus two. Minus one clears it; minus five does not.
